==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|arriven}}, {{m|enm|ariven}}, from {{der|en|fro|ariver}}, from {{der|en|la-eme|adripo|adrīpāre|t=to land, come ashore}}, derived from {{der|en|la|rīpa|t=shore, river-bank}}. Displaced native {{m|en|oncome}}, {{m|sco|tocome}}.

For the semantic evolution, compare {{cog|ang|ġelandian}}, {{m|ang|ġelendan}}, {{m|ang|lendan|t=to arrive at land; land}} > Middle English {{m|enm|alenden}}, {{m|enm|landen|t=to arrive; arrive at shore; land}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ə-rīvʹ}}, {{IPA|en|/əˈɹaɪv/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-arrive.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪv|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative}} To [[reach]]; to get to a certain place.
#: {{syn|en|fetch up}}
#: {{ux|en|We've just '''arrived''' at the hotel to book in, so we should '''arrive''' at Mike’s in time for lunch.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''arrived''' home for two days.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=No hiding place| date=2013-05-25| volume=407| issue=8837| page=74| url=http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no| passage=In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the physical and electronic varieties—last year. Yet of those who received unsolicited adverts through the post, only 3% bought anything as a result. If the bumf '''arrived''' electronically, the take-up rate was 0.1%. And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025020559/https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no|archivedate=25 October 2017}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[obtain]] a [[level]] of [[success]] or [[fame]]; to [[succeed]].
#: {{ux|en|He had finally '''arrived''' on Broadway.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Donald Cole|title=Immigrant City: Lawrence, Massachusetts, 1845-1921|page=58
|passage=Evidence that the Irish had '''arrived''' socially was the abrupt decline in the number of newspaper articles accusing them of brawling and other crimes.}}
# {{lbl|en|intransitive}} To come; said of time.
#: {{ux|en|The time has '''arrived''' for us to depart.}}
# {{lbl|en|intransitive}} To happen or occur.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1666|author=w:Edmund Waller|title=Instructions to a Painter
|passage=Happy! to whom this glorious death '''arrives'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|orgasm}}{{lb|en|intransitive|often vulgar|slang|chiefly|UK|Ireland}} To achieve [[orgasm]]; to [[cum #Verb|cum]]; to [[ejaculate]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To reach; to come to.
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=II|passage=Ere he '''arrive''' the happy isle.|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|I|ii|passage=Ere we could '''arrive''' the point proposed.}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|text='''Arrive''' at last the blessed goal.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To bring to [[shore]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1618|author=w:George Chapman|title=A Hymn to Apollo
|passage=and made the sea-trod ship '''arrive''' them}}

====Usage notes====
* Additional, nonstandard, and uncommon past tense and past participle are, respectively, {{m|en|arrove}} and {{m|en|arriven}}, formed by analogy to verbs like {{m|en|drove}} and {{m|en|driven}}.

====Antonyms====
* {{l|en|depart}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|arrivage|arrivance|arrivant|arrive at|it is better to travel hopefully than to arrive|rearrive|unarrived|unarriving}}

====Related terms====
* {{l|en|arrival}}
